doc.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Time magazine cover and Ellington's knock on the door
summary: The 1954 Time cover brought backlash and benefits, and Duke woke him in Denver with the issue.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: November 8th, 1954. Your picture’s on the cover of Time magazine. How did that impact your career? Did this – for good or for bad. Did it change your life?
There’s rumors that it’s not all gravy.
There was a backlash, I would imagine.

Yeah, a backlash for sure. There’s stories abound that the bad luck that somebody had after being on the cover, or bad criticism. That did happen to a certain degree. But to balance it, the good that comes from it balances any – by far, the good is far better than then negative.
Is it true that you were on the road in the same city as Duke Ellington the day that [ ] story?

Touring with the Duke Ellington band. I believe we were in Denver at the time. There was a knock on my door, seven in the morning. There’s Duke Ellington with Time magazine, saying, “Dave, you’re on the cover.”
What a remarkable way to find out.
I was hoping – because I knew they were doing a story on both of us – that Duke would come first, as he should. There it was. There was no way. But soon Ellington was on the cover.
